parameters.name: jacket_closure
parameters.description: Whether the jacket front is single-breasted or double-breasted, affecting formality and visual width

values.definition: Single row of buttons with a narrow overlap. More versatile, can be worn open or closed. Slimmer silhouette.
Two parallel rows of buttons with wide overlap. Incrementally more stylish than single-breasted. Pointed diagonal lapels dress up any worsted. Should be worn buttoned. Projects broader chest.

parameters.visual_effect: DB adds visual width to torso and projects formality. SB is more neutral and versatile.

parameters.name: jacket_button_configuration
parameters.description: Number and arrangement of front buttons on the jacket, affecting the V-opening and visual proportions

values.definition: Single button, lowest stance. Maximum V-opening exposing furnishings. Most elongating. Typically reserved for formal/dinner jackets.
Most popular modern configuration. Lower button stance than three-button, showing more shirt and tie. Gives trimmer look with defined waistline via darts.
Higher button stance, less V-opening. Classic conservative look. Top button optional (often rolled). Shortens perceived torso length.
Three-button jacket where the top button is hidden under a soft lapel roll. Combines the height of a 3-button with the openness of a 2-button. Neapolitan style.
Most common double-breasted: 6 front buttons, 2 that fasten. Broad lapels mark a high waist, straight tails hug hips. Classic DB configuration.
6 front buttons, only bottom one fastens. Lapels roll down below waist, giving illusion of height. Known as the 'Kent' style after Duke of Kent.
4 front buttons, 2 that fasten. More relaxed, laid-back double-breasted look.

parameters.visual_effect: Higher button stance = shorter perceived torso. Lower stance = more elongating. The V-opening frames the shirt/tie and draws the eye upward to the face.

parameters.name: lapel_style
parameters.description: Shape of the jacket lapel, affecting formality and the framing of the face/chest area

values.definition: Standard lapel with a triangular notch where collar meets lapel. Most common on single-breasted jackets. Neutral formality.

Pointed lapels that angle upward toward the shoulders. Standard on double-breasted jackets. On single-breasted, it virtually neutralizes the DB's edge in formality. Spearheaded the popularity of the V-shaped male chest.
Continuous rounded lapel with no notch or peak. Reserved for dinner jackets and tuxedos. Most formal.

parameters.visual_effect: Peak lapels widen the chest visually and direct the eye outward/upward. Notch is neutral. Shawl creates a smooth, formal line.

parameters.name: lapel_width
parameters.description: Width of the jacket lapel measured at its widest point, which should harmonize with tie width and collar spread

values.definition: Under 3 inches. Slims the chest area. Fashion-forward or casual.
3 to 3.5 inches. Classic proportion. Harmonizes with standard tie width.
Over 3.5 inches. Broadens the chest. More traditional/powerful look.

parameters.visual_effect: Wider lapels add visual breadth to the chest. Should match tie width for visual harmony. Rule: lapel width ≈ tie width ≈ collar spread.

parameters.name: gorge_height
parameters.description: Position of the collar-lapel junction (gorge) on the jacket, affecting perceived shoulder line and modernity

values.definition: Below the collarbone. Vintage/classic look. Elongates the lapel line.
At or near the collarbone/shoulder line. Timeless positioning.
Above the shoulder line. Contemporary Italian style. Creates a more modern, shorter lapel look.

parameters.visual_effect: Higher gorge creates a more contemporary look and can make the wearer appear taller. Lower gorge is more classic.

parameters.name: jacket_shoulder_type
parameters.description: Construction and shape of the jacket shoulder, significantly affecting the silhouette and perceived body shape

values.definition: Built-up shoulder with padding. Creates a defined, broad shoulder line. British tradition. Projects authority and width.
Minimal or no padding, following the body's natural shoulder line. American Ivy League/sack suit tradition. Also Neapolitan 'spalla camicia' (shirt shoulder).
Slightly extended with a raised ridge at the sleevehead (spalla con rollino). Neapolitan tradition. Adds subtle width without bulk.
Shoulder line extends beyond the natural shoulder point. Creates illusion of broader shoulders.
Concave/saddle-shaped shoulder (spalla insellata). Dramatic Neapolitan detail.

parameters.visual_effect: Structured shoulders broaden a narrow frame. Soft shoulders suit already-broad shoulders. Extended/padded shoulders add visual width.

parameters.name: jacket_vent_style
parameters.description: Slit(s) at the back of the jacket affecting movement, silhouette, and formality

values.definition: No slit in back. Clean, trim contour. Dressier. But bunches up when sitting or reaching into pockets. Between the wars, most bespoke lounge suits and dinner jackets were ventless.

Single slit at center back. American predilection, Ivy League look. Least expensive to manufacture. Pulls open like a garage door when hand reaches for pocket, revealing the derriere. Least stylish option per Flusser.

Two slits on either side. Highest union of function and form. Permits pocket access while covering buttocks. Leads the eye up either side, imbuing illusion of greater height. Subtle concert of motion between vents and trousers lends fluidity and grace. British tradition.

parameters.visual_effect: Side vents elongate and add grace to movement. Ventless is sleek but restrictive. Center vent is functional but inelegant.

parameters.name: jacket_pocket_type
parameters.description: Style of the jacket's lower pockets, affecting formality and visual bulk

values.definition: Narrow welted slit pockets with no flap. Most formal. Clean, sleek surface. Used on tuxedos and dressier suits. Double-besom construction is the highest quality.
Pockets with a fabric flap covering the opening. Standard formality. Flaps add a layer of fabric, making the jacket slightly less sleek. Can be tucked in for a cleaner look.
Pockets sewn onto the jacket's surface. Most casual. Add another layer to the surface. Would be a sartorial oxymoron on a dark pinstriped suit. Appropriate for sport jackets and light-colored suits.
Diagonally angled flap pockets. Originally from riding/hacking jackets. Chisels breadth away from the hip while adding a line of height. Sporty, slightly Anglicized character.

parameters.notes: Ticket/cash pocket: small extra pocket above the lower hip pocket. Flapped version diminishes dressiness; besom version heightens it.

parameters.name: jacket_silhouette
parameters.description: The overall cut tradition of the jacket, determined by the combination of shoulder, waist, and drape characteristics
parameters.note: This parameter is the canonical owner of silhouette/tailoring tradition concepts. D02 and D06 reference this parameter.

values.definition: British/Savile Row tradition. Structured, padded shoulders, fuller chest with drape, suppressed waist, close-fitting hip. Side vents. Also known as 'structured' silhouette. The driving force behind tailored fashion in the 1920s-30s.

American/Ivy League tradition. Natural/unpadded shoulders, undarted straight-hanging body, minimal waist suppression. Soft rolled lapels, three-button front. Brooks Brothers signature. Also known as 'natural' silhouette.

Italian tradition. Soft/minimal shoulder padding, low gorge, lightweight construction. Ranges from Neapolitan (unstructured, spalla camicia) to Milanese (clean, precise). Also known as 'soft/draped' silhouette. Generally lighter and more body-conscious.

parameters.visual_effect: British drape creates a V-shaped athletic silhouette. American sack is relaxed and straight. Italian is body-conscious and light.

parameters.name: jacket_sleeve_buttons
parameters.description: Number of buttons on the jacket sleeve cuff, a subtle marker of sartorial attention

values.definition: Minimal, clean. Acceptable on two-button jackets.
Often used on summer/lighter jackets. Harmonizes with three-button front.
Standard on suit jackets. Conveys superior sartorial breeding per London tradition. Buttons set close together with edges 'kissing.'

parameters.notes: Working/surgeon's cuffs (functional buttonholes) are a bespoke marker. Bottom button should finish no more than 3/4 inch above the sleeve bottom.

parameters.name: jacket_construction
parameters.description: Internal construction method affecting drape, shape retention, and quality

values.definition: Interlining glued to outer fabric. Budget construction. Can bubble over time. Less natural drape.
Canvas interlining in upper chest and lapels only. Good balance of quality and cost. Lapels roll naturally.
Canvas throughout entire front panel. Highest quality. Molds to the wearer's body over time. Best drape and shape retention.

parameters.visual_effect: Full canvas creates the most natural, fluid drape. Fused jackets appear stiffer and less organic.

parameters.name: jacket_formality_tier
parameters.description: Hierarchical formality ranking of tailored upper garments

values.definition: Matched with trousers of same fabric. Highest formality in daily wear. Should not be worn as a standalone piece.

Ranks between suit and sport jacket in dressiness. Metal buttons (brass/gilt/nickel/mother-of-pearl). Chameleon-like versatility — works with flannels, jeans, shorts. DB blazer is slightly more formal than SB.
Most casual of tailored jackets. 'Odd' detailing: bellows pleats, action backs, patch pockets, bold patterns. Not meant to be mistaken for a suit jacket.

parameters.notes: Within each tier: DB > SB, flap pockets > patch, peaked lapels > notched, side vents > center vent, dark trousers > light trousers — each increments formality.

parameters.name: trouser_front
parameters.description: Whether trousers have pleats and their configuration, affecting comfort, drape, and formality

values.definition: No pleats. Clean, slim appearance. Pared-down, uncluttered simplicity. Low rise and form-fitting contour.
One pleat on each side. Moderate fullness.

Two pleats on each side — a deep one near the fly and a shallower one toward the pocket. Classic design. The smaller pleat helps the larger one remain closed. More than two pleats is a fashion gimmick.
Pleat folds face toward the fly/center. Traditional English style.
Pleat folds face toward the pocket/side seam. Most common in ready-to-wear.

parameters.visual_effect: Pleats look dressier and provide comfort. Flat-front is slimmer and more modern. Pleats accommodate hip widening when seated.

parameters.name: trouser_rise
parameters.description: Distance from crotch seam to waistband top, determining where trousers sit on the body

values.definition: Sits at the natural waist (near navel). Classical positioning. Returned in the 1980s with pleats and suspenders. Creates ideal balance between jacket and trousers.
Sits between natural waist and hip bones. Modern standard for most ready-to-wear.
Sits at or below the hip bones. If waistband rests between natural waist and hip, the ideal balance between jacket and trousers is doomed per Flusser.

parameters.visual_effect: High rise elongates the legs visually. Low rise shortens the leg line and can cause jacket-trouser proportion imbalance.

parameters.name: trouser_break
parameters.description: Amount of fabric that folds at the front crease where the trouser meets the shoe

values.definition: Hem just above the shoe with no horizontal fold. Clean, modern, slightly shorter appearance.
Minor horizontal crease/dimple where trouser meets shoe. Most versatile and recommended.
Moderate fold of fabric over the shoe. Traditional business standard.
Significant fabric pooling on the shoe. More casual, can look sloppy if unintentional.

parameters.visual_effect: Less break creates a cleaner, more elongating line. Full break can shorten apparent leg length.

parameters.name: trouser_cuff
parameters.description: Whether trouser hems are turned up (cuffed) or left plain, affecting visual weight at the ankle

values.definition: Trouser hem turned up, typically 1.5-2 inches. Adds visual weight at the bottom. Helps the trouser hang straight. Cuffed bottoms and crease significantly improve the line of a trouser. Not used on formal trousers.
Plain hem with no turn-up. Required for formal wear. Creates a slightly longer, uninterrupted leg line.

parameters.visual_effect: Cuffs add horizontal line at ankle (shortening effect) but also weight that improves drape. Short men should use narrower cuffs or skip them.

parameters.name: trouser_width
parameters.description: Width of the trouser leg, particularly at the knee and hem

values.definition: Tapered, body-conscious cut. Modern/fashion-forward. Narrower through thigh and hem.
Medium width with gentle taper from thigh to hem. Classic proportion.

Generous width allowing natural drape and movement. Full across hip and thigh, tapering to bottom. Classical tailoring tradition. Long, wide trousers supported the columnar, athletic silhouette of the 1920s-30s.

parameters.visual_effect: Fuller trousers add volume and can balance a broader upper body. Slim trousers elongate but expose leg shape.

parameters.name: trouser_waistband
parameters.description: Fastening method at the trouser waist, affecting silhouette and formality

values.definition: Standard loops for a belt, 1.25 to 1.5 inch width. Most common modern construction.
Tab adjusters on either side of the waist. Cleaner waistline without belt bulk. Also known as side tabs.
Buttons inside waistband for braces/suspenders. Allows trousers to hang from shoulders. Cleaner drape.
Matching fabric belt integrated into the waistband. Removed the bother of a separate belt. Popular for resort and casual wear. Fastened with D-ring.
Self-supporting beltless trouser with internal elastic and side tabs. First self-supporting beltless trouser, invented 1932. Comfort-in-action design.
One-piece front and back with narrow belt loops positioned below the trouser's top. Created in the 1930s. Requires narrow belts.

parameters.name: shirt_collar_style
parameters.description: Shape and style of the dress shirt collar, which frames the face and must harmonize with face shape, tie knot, and jacket lapels

values.definition: Standard collar with points angled downward. Most stylisticaly neutral. Points should be 2.75 to 3.375 inches long. Narrow opening between points favors a rounder, oval face rather than narrow one.

Collar points spread apart at a wider angle. Keystone of the English bespoke look since the 1920s. Inherently dressy and elegant. Wider spread counters narrow faces. Several models available to flatter any head shape.
Extreme spread where points angle almost horizontally or backward. Most formal spread variant. Also called Windsor collar.

Collar points fastened to shirt front with buttons. American contribution to dress shirt fashion. Quintessential Ivy League. Can be dressed up or down. Less formal than other collar types. Projects casual elegance.

Collar with small fabric tabs that connect behind the tie knot, pushing the knot up and forward. Raises the tie knot higher on the neck. Functions like a pin collar. Adds extra measure of nattiness but demands precision in execution.

Collar points connected by a decorative pin underneath the tie knot. Raises the knot, creating an elegant arch in the tie. Demands a bit more aplomb. Once worn by half of all American men. Pointed ends work to counterpoint the rounded or oval contour of chin.
Collar with rounded points instead of sharp ones. Vintage style. Originated in Eton College. Less common today.
Small standing collar with folded-down tips (wings). Reserved for formal evening wear with bow ties.

parameters.visual_effect: Collar frames the face like a picture frame. Spread collars widen a narrow face. Point collars narrow a wide face. Collar height must suit neck length — longer necks need higher collars. Small collars make a large head appear larger.

parameters.name: shirt_collar_height
parameters.description: Height of the collar band that sits around the neck, which must relate to the wearer's neck length

values.definition: Short collar band sitting lower on the neck. Casual. Can make neck appear longer.
Medium height collar band. Appropriate for most neck lengths.
Higher collar band sitting higher on the neck. More formal. Italian tradition. Long necklines require higher-sitting collars to maintain proper proportion.

parameters.visual_effect: Collar height should be proportional to neck length. A long neck is best balanced by a higher collar. A short neck needs a lower collar to avoid looking compressed.

parameters.name: shirt_collar_stiffness
parameters.description: The firmness or softness of the collar fabric, affecting its drape and formality

values.definition: Unfused, natural drape. Casual feel. Pairs with natural-shoulder jackets. Button-down collars are inherently soft.
Light interlining for some structure. Most versatile.
Heavily fused or starched for crisp, formal appearance. A full face that sags around chin or cheeks demands a stiffer collar to counteract effects of age and gravity.

parameters.name: shirt_cuff_style
parameters.description: Style of the shirt sleeve cuff, affecting formality and what accessories are worn

values.definition: Standard button cuff. Can have 1-3 buttons. Most common and versatile. Less formal.
Folded-back cuff fastened with cufflinks. More formal. The 'showing linen' — exposing shirt cuff at the wrist — was historically a sign of gentility.
Can be fastened with either buttons or cufflinks. Versatile.

parameters.visual_effect: Shirt cuffs should show 1/2 to 3/4 inch below jacket sleeve. This 'showing linen' at the wrist is one of Flusser's 5 key body intersections.

parameters.name: tie_knot_type
parameters.description: Method used to tie the necktie, producing different knot sizes and shapes that must harmonize with collar spread

values.definition: Small, slightly asymmetrical knot. Most versatile and classic. Works best with point and button-down collars. Uses least tie length.
Medium, symmetrical triangular knot. Works well with spread and semi-spread collars.
Large, symmetrical triangular knot. Designed for wide spread/cutaway collars. Flusser warns against its bulbous mass forcing truncated collar points farther off the chest.
Medium, symmetrical knot tied inside-out. Good alternative to Half-Windsor.

parameters.visual_effect: Knot size must fill the collar opening — outer borders of tie knot should correspond with inner borders of the collar. Too-small knot in wide spread looks lost; too-large knot in narrow collar forces points apart.

parameters.name: tie_width
parameters.description: Width of the necktie blade at its widest point, which should harmonize with lapel width

values.definition: Under 2.5 inches. Fashion-forward, casual. Pairs with narrow lapels.
2.5 to 3 inches. Modern proportion.
3.25 to 3.5 inches. Classic width. Harmonizes with standard lapels.
Over 3.5 inches. Traditional/vintage proportion.

parameters.visual_effect: Tie width should roughly match jacket lapel width for visual harmony. Mismatched widths create visual imbalance.

parameters.name: tie_length
parameters.description: Where the tie blade tip terminates relative to the waistband

values.definition: Tip reaches the trouser waistband or belt buckle center. Ideal length. Both blades should be close in length.
Tip ends above the belt. Too short. Exposes the narrow end behind.
Tip hangs below the belt. Too long. Looks sloppy and shortens the torso visually.

parameters.name: tie_dimple
parameters.description: Whether the tie has a pinched crease/dimple just below the knot

values.definition: Pinched crease below the knot creating a small indentation. Adds dimension, texture, and elegance. Sign of sartorial attention.
Flat, smooth tie below the knot. Simpler, less fussy.

parameters.name: suit_piece_count
parameters.description: Number of matched pieces in the suit ensemble

values.definition: Jacket and matching trousers. Modern standard.

Jacket, matching trousers, and matching waistcoat/vest. The waistcoat adds gravitas, holds tie in place, keeps shirt tidy, lends efficient appearance when in shirtsleeves. Prior to WWII, most suits were three-piece.

parameters.visual_effect: Waistcoat adds a layer of formality, covers the trouser waistband, and provides additional opportunity for visual interest via odd waistcoats.

parameters.name: blazer_button_material
parameters.description: Material of blazer buttons, affecting formality and character

values.definition: Traditional blazer button. Classiest is plain, flat English gilt with shank. Implies gentility and tradition.
Dulled nickel or pewter shade. Good for men with gray hair or predominantly gray-toned trousers.
Off-white buttons. Option for brighter blue tropical wool or linen blazers.
Dark brown horn. First non-metal alternative considered. But its dullish character lacks personality to offset the dark jacket.

parameters.name: tshirt_neckline
parameters.description: The shape and style of the neckline opening on a t-shirt, which determines formality, comfort, visual proportion, and suitability for different face/body shapes

values.definition: A close-fitting, round neckline that sits at the base of the neck with a ribbed collar providing elasticity and shape retention. The most universal and classic t-shirt neckline, originating from 1930s U.S. Navy undershirts. Suits virtually all body types.

A neckline that dips into a sharp V shape at the center front, creating visual length and elongating the neck. Depth varies from shallow to deep cuts. Reinforced seams around the V-cut prevent sagging. Particularly flattering for rounder faces and broader builds as it visually slims the appearance.

A round neckline with a buttoned placket (typically 2-5 buttons, 3-5 inch length) extending down the chest. A hybrid between crew neck and polo shirt, originating from rowers in Henley-on-Thames in the 1800s. More elevated than a standard tee but less formal than a polo, offering adjustable ventilation through the button placket.

A broader, U-shaped neckline that dips lower and wider than a crew neck, revealing more of the collarbone. Offers a relaxed, modern aesthetic that is both casual and contemporary. The wider and deeper cut provides excellent comfort and breathability, making it a favorite for summer wear.

A collar that rises 1-2 inches above the base of the neck without extending to a full turtleneck height. Sits close to the neck creating a sleek, sophisticated silhouette. Splits the difference between a crew neck and a full turtleneck. Works well as a standalone piece or layered under jackets.

A horizontal neckline running across the collarbones from shoulder to shoulder, skimming the collarbones and accentuating the shoulders. Rooted in 1930s French nautical wear and popularized by Coco Chanel. Requires strong shoulder seams to maintain structure. Can visually widen narrow shoulders.

A high, close-fitting collar that folds over and covers the entire neck, typically extending 3-4 inches above the base. Provides maximum neck coverage and warmth, suitable for cold weather. Creates a refined, intellectual aesthetic often associated with smart casual to semi-formal styling.

A fold-over collar with a buttoned placket, combining the comfort of a t-shirt with the structure of a collared shirt. Associated with sporty elegance and smart-casual dressing. The collar provides formality that round-neck tees lack.

A small V-shaped cut at the center of an otherwise round neckline, typically only 1-2 inches deep. Provides a subtle detail that differentiates from a plain crew neck while remaining understated and versatile.

A round neckline featuring a small, teardrop or keyhole-shaped opening at the front, sometimes secured with a button or loop. Adds visual interest to an otherwise simple neckline while maintaining modesty.
A neckline with a short vertical opening at the center front, similar to a henley but without buttons. Creates a casual, slightly open appearance that offers more breathability than a crew neck.

parameters.name: tshirt_fit
parameters.description: The overall silhouette and cut of a t-shirt relative to the wearer's body, determining how closely the garment follows the body's contours and how much ease (extra fabric) is built in

values.definition: Sits closer to the body from chest to waist with narrower sleeves and minimal extra fabric. Follows the natural body shape more tightly than regular fit, emphasizing the torso's definition. Best suited for lean to average builds. Creates a sharper, more tailored casual appearance.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: A straight, classic cut that sits close to the body without clinging. The middle-of-the-road approach with standard proportions: not too tight, not too loose. The most versatile fit suitable for all-day comfort across most body types. Often used interchangeably with 'standard fit' or 'classic fit'.

The middle ground between regular and oversized. Offers extra space around the chest, shoulders, and sleeves while still following the wearer's frame. Drapes away from the body slightly without entering oversized territory, providing comfort and ease of movement.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: Significantly larger than the wearer's typical size, creating a baggy, drapey silhouette. Features more fabric everywhere, especially in body length and sleeve drop. Popular in streetwear and hip-hop fashion. Often several sizes up from usual, with dropped shoulders and extended length.

A form-fitting cut designed to closely follow the contours of a muscular physique. Tight-fitting around the chest and waist with sleeves that hug the biceps, but may have slightly more room in the shoulders compared to slim fit. Emphasizes chest, shoulders, and arms.

Features an extended hemline that typically reaches past the hips, sometimes to mid-thigh. The body fit can be slim, standard, or relaxed, but the defining characteristic is the extra length. Particularly flattering on taller individuals and useful for covering the hip and thigh area.

A square-shaped cut that is wide through the torso and sleeves, hanging straight down from the shoulders without tapering. Features minimal body contouring with a wider, squarer silhouette. Unlike oversized, boxy tees are not necessarily long and do not typically have dropped shoulders; they focus on horizontal volume, often with a slightly cropped length.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: A tapered fit with more room through the chest and shoulders that narrows at the waist, accommodating a V-shaped torso. Designed for athletic builds (broad shoulders, defined chest, tapered waist) without being excessively tight. Ideal for layering under blazers or sweaters.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

parameters.name: tshirt_sleeve_length
parameters.description: The length and style of the sleeve on a t-shirt, affecting coverage, formality, seasonal suitability, and visual proportions of the arm

values.definition: Completely removes the sleeve, leaving the upper arms fully exposed. Also called tank tops or muscle shirts. Ideal for workouts, beach days, or casual summer outfits. Maximizes freedom of movement and keeps the wearer cool in hot weather.
sources: Fabriclore - Men T-Shirt Sleeve Styles Guide

values.definition: Covers only the top of the shoulder, shorter than standard short sleeves. Adds an edgy, trendy touch best suited for men with toned arms as it highlights biceps and shoulders. More common in women's styles but increasingly seen in men's activewear and summer fashion.
sources: Fabriclore - Men T-Shirt Sleeve Styles Guide

values.definition: The most common and traditional t-shirt sleeve length, covering approximately half of the upper arm. Length varies slightly depending on design and can be more or less fitted. Often called 'regular sleeves' as it is the default for both men's and women's t-shirts. Universally versatile across seasons and occasions.
sources: Fabriclore - Men T-Shirt Sleeve Styles Guide

values.definition: Hits between the elbow and wrist, covering approximately three-quarters of the arm. Commonly associated with baseball/raglan tees. A great transitional piece for unpredictable weather, providing more coverage than short sleeves while remaining lighter than full long sleeves. Visually elongates the arms.
sources: Fabriclore - Men T-Shirt Sleeve Styles Guide

values.definition: Extends all the way to the wrist, providing full arm coverage from a single layer of lightweight fabric. Can end in a ribbed cuff that is tighter around the wrist (more common in men's styles) or have a looser, open wrist. Ideal for cooler weather while maintaining the casual comfort of a t-shirt.
sources: Fabriclore - Men T-Shirt Sleeve Styles Guide

values.definition: Short sleeves that are folded or rolled up once or twice for a more casual, relaxed appearance. Often pre-stitched in the rolled position. Gives a slightly shorter, more intentional look than standard short sleeves and adds textural detail to the silhouette.

parameters.name: tshirt_fabric_weight
parameters.description: The weight of the t-shirt fabric measured in GSM (grams per square meter) or oz/yd2 (ounces per square yard), directly affecting drape, opacity, durability, warmth, and seasonal suitability

values.definition: 120-150 GSM (3.5-4.5 oz/yd2). Thinner, breathable fabric that drapes naturally. Ideal for summer, hot climates, layering, or a casual slouchy look. Dries quickly but wrinkles more easily. May be more transparent and prone to shrinkage. Best for warm weather and athletic applications.

150-180 GSM (4.5-5.3 oz/yd2). The 'Goldilocks' range offering the best balance of comfort, durability, and professional appearance. Suitable for year-round and mid-season wear. Works well with all printing techniques (DTG, sublimation, screen printing). The most commonly recommended weight for everyday t-shirts.

180-200+ GSM (5.3-6+ oz/yd2). Thicker, sturdier fabric with a substantial, premium feel. Highly durable, resists wear and tear from frequent washing, and retains shape over many laundry cycles. Better suited for cooler fall/winter weather or workwear. Provides superior opacity and structure. Popular in streetwear and premium basics.

220+ GSM (6.5+ oz/yd2). The thickest, most substantial t-shirt fabric weight. Extremely durable with a rigid, structured feel. Most commonly found in premium streetwear and designer basics. Provides maximum opacity and a distinctly luxurious hand feel. Very warm, best for cold weather.

parameters.name: polo_collar_type
parameters.description: The style, construction, and material of the collar on a polo shirt, affecting formality, structure, and visual character of the garment

values.definition: The standard polo collar made from ribbed knit fabric, creating a distinct pattern of vertical lines. The ribbed construction provides elasticity, shape retention, and a subtle textured sophistication. Introduced in the 1970s, it is the most common polo collar type. Designed to stand up against the neck and frame the face when worn properly.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles

values.definition: A polo collar whose points are anchored to the shirt body by small buttons, creating a billowing effect known as a 'collar roll'. Originally invented for polo players to keep collar points from moving during matches. Associated with preppy style and offers a more secure, windproof collar that stays in place during activity.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A short, stand-up collar (band collar) without the traditional fold-over points. Does not meet at the front, creating a clean, minimalist look. Named after Imperial China's Mandarin officials. Also called a band collar, Mao collar, or grandad collar. Creates a modern, Asian-inspired aesthetic that works in both casual and contemporary settings.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A collar with wide-set points, creating more space between the collar tips than a classic point collar. Borrowed from dress shirt styling, the spread collar on a polo creates a smarter, more formal appearance. Often combined with slim-fit shirts for a dressier casual look.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles

values.definition: A polo collar featuring contrast-colored stripes or piping along the edge of the collar (and often matching at the cuffs). The tipping detail adds visual interest, color accent, and a sporting heritage reference. A hallmark of classic British and tennis-inspired polo styling.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A polo collar made from a fabric or color entirely different from the shirt body. Offers a bold visual statement where the collar becomes a distinct design element. Popular since the 1980s-90s and continues to evolve with modern interpretations pairing different textures and colors.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles

values.definition: A collar constructed from the same fabric as the shirt body rather than ribbed knit. Often includes sewn-in collar stays and a collar stand for structure. Creates a smoother, more uniform appearance. Common on performance and polyester polos; less expensive to manufacture than ribbed knit collars.
sources: All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles

values.definition: A collar made from woven (non-knit) fabric attached to a knit polo body. Bridges the gap between a polo and a dress shirt, providing the crispness and formality of a woven collar with the comfort of a knit body. Often seen on dress-code-friendly polos.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A polo-style shirt that completely omits a collar, presenting a clean neckline similar to a crew-neck t-shirt but retaining other polo elements like a button placket. Offers a minimalist, modern alternative for those who prefer a pared-back aesthetic.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts
All Seasons Uniforms - Polo Collar Styles

parameters.name: polo_fabric
parameters.description: The knit construction and fiber composition of a polo shirt fabric, determining texture, weight, breathability, structure, and occasion suitability

values.definition: A textured, double-weave knit with a distinctive waffle or honeycomb surface. Invented by Rene Lacoste in 1926 for tennis. Medium weight with 8-12% natural elasticity. The micro-chambers in the weave trap air for insulation while allowing vapor escape, providing excellent moisture-wicking. Holds shape well, resists creases, and conceals perspiration. The classic polo fabric ideal for business casual and smart settings. Best for embroidery.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide
Moda Knits - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A smooth, flat, single-knit fabric that is lightweight and soft to the touch. Has 15-25% natural mechanical stretch. Feels like a favorite t-shirt with a polo's structured collar. Revolutionized by Coco Chanel in the 1910s. More casual than pique, lighter weight, wrinkles less, and drapes more naturally. Better for physical activity, warmer climates, and travel. Works well for screen printing.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide
Moda Knits - Types of Polo Shirts
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A dense, double-layered knit produced by two rows of stitches interwoven together. Heavier than pique with a stretchy, comfortable fit and a more luxurious feel. Drapes more elegantly and is less prone to wrinkling. The thicker construction provides superior insulation, making it ideal for cooler weather, loungewear, and cold-weather layering.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide
Moda Knits - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A blend combining cotton's natural breathability with silk's softness and subtle sheen. Creates a lightweight, elegant feel that transitions easily from casual to elevated occasions. The silk component adds a luxurious hand-feel and slight luster that differentiates it from standard cotton polos. Particularly suited for Indian smart-casual dressing.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide

values.definition: Engineered synthetic or blended fabrics (often polyester, spandex, nylon) designed for athletic and active wear. Features include moisture-wicking, quick-dry capability, anti-odor properties, UV protection (UPF30+), wrinkle resistance, shape retention, and built-in stretch. May contain reflective elements. Typically slim-fitted for sport applications.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: Cotton yarn that has undergone a mercerization treatment creating a permanent luster and subtle sheen. The process also improves dye uptake, color fastness, and fabric strength. Results in a smooth, polished appearance that pairs well with dress trousers. Dominates the business casual polo space alongside fine-gauge knits.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A variation of pique where multiple threads are bundled together during knitting. Can combine different fibers (expensive + affordable), strengthen fabric through thread doubling, or create a subtle mottled color effect by knitting two colored threads together. Heavier and more substantial than standard pique.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide
Moda Knits - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A blended fabric combining cotton's breathability and comfort with polyester's durability, wrinkle resistance, and color retention. Dries faster than pure cotton and holds shape well after many washes. Widely used in Indian market polo shirts for its balance of comfort and easy maintenance. Common in sport, uniform, and everyday categories.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide

values.definition: A polo constructed from fine-gauge knitted wool or merino wool, offering warmth, texture, and a vintage-inspired aesthetic. Straddles the line between casual and formal, providing more structure than cotton knits. Heavier than standard polo fabrics, best suited for autumn/winter wear.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

parameters.name: polo_fit
parameters.description: The overall silhouette and cut of a polo shirt relative to the wearer's body, from trim and body-hugging to loose and comfortable

values.definition: The trimmest silhouette with sleeves that hug the bicep and a slim cut through the chest and waist. Sits closer to the body, emphasizing the torso's shape and definition without excess material around the waist or hips. Best for leaner physiques. Creates the most tailored, modern casual appearance.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: A trim silhouette positioned between classic and slim fit. The sleeve hugs the bicep and the shirt is tailored through the waist but with slightly more room than a full slim fit. Offers a tailored shape without being too tight, making it versatile for almost any body type.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: The roomiest silhouette with a lower armhole and a fuller sleeve that falls closer to the elbow. Provides more room in the chest, arms, and waist without clinging. Highly versatile, suiting most body types, particularly broader builds. Allows better air circulation, making it comfortable for hot weather. Follows the body's contours without hugging.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: A looser fit than classic with a more relaxed opening through the shoulder, chest, and waist. Standard sleeve length finishing just above the elbow with a wider sleeve opening. Prioritizes comfort and ease of movement over a tailored silhouette. Ideal for casual, off-duty wear.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

values.definition: Designed for athletic or V-shaped builds with broad shoulders and a tapered waist. Provides more room in the chest and shoulders while narrowing at the midsection. Accommodates muscular physiques without excess fabric in the waist area, creating a clean silhouette that follows the body's natural taper.
sources: Tapered Menswear - Polo Classic vs Slim Fit

parameters.name: polo_placket
parameters.description: The reinforced strip at the front opening of a polo shirt where the buttonholes and buttons are located, including button count and construction style. The placket frames the neckline and affects how open or controlled the collar appears.

values.definition: A placket with two buttons, providing a slightly more laid-back and casual appearance. Creates a shorter placket opening. Ideal for relaxed, leisure-oriented occasions and warm-weather wear. The reduced button count gives a cleaner, more minimal front appearance.
sources: Polo Shirts Only - Decoding Fits Collars Plackets

values.definition: The most popular and versatile placket style, considered the classic polo standard. Three buttons provide enough structure to look polished while maintaining a sporty feel. Holds the center front visually and works for more customers, body types, and occasions than any other button count. Often sells best in retail settings.
sources: Polo Shirts Only - Decoding Fits Collars Plackets

values.definition: A longer placket with four buttons, signaling heritage, premium intent, or a signature design detail. Creates a deeper front opening that can be worn partially unbuttoned for a relaxed look. Less common than two or three-button versions, often seen on designer or rugby-influenced polos.

Also called a fly-front or concealed placket. Features an extra layer of fabric that covers the buttons underneath, hiding all fasteners and creating a clean, smooth line down the front. Produces the most polished, minimal appearance with no visible openings or stitching. Common on dressier, designer, and fashion-forward polos.
sources: Polo Shirts Only - Decoding Fits Collars Plackets

values.definition: Replaces the traditional button placket with a zipper closure, offering quick adjustability and a sporty, modern aesthetic. Common on performance and activewear polos. Can range from a short quarter-zip to a full-length zip. Adds a functional, technical character to the garment.
sources: Polo Shirts Only - Decoding Fits Collars Plackets
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: Uses snap fasteners instead of buttons or zippers for a quick-open, quick-close mechanism. Often found on performance and utility-oriented polos. Provides a clean front appearance when closed and allows rapid ventilation adjustment.
sources: Polo Shirts Only - Decoding Fits Collars Plackets

parameters.name: polo_sleeve_length
parameters.description: The length of the sleeve on a polo shirt, affecting seasonal suitability, formality, and styling versatility

values.definition: The standard polo sleeve length, ending at or just above mid-bicep. The most common and classic option, suitable for warm weather and the majority of polo shirt styling scenarios. Sleeve should be snug but not restricting, ideally finishing at the mid-point of the upper arm.

Extends to the wrist, providing full arm coverage. Ideal for cooler temperatures, transitional weather, and more elevated styling. Long-sleeve polos bridge the gap between a standard polo and an Oxford cloth button-down shirt (OCBD). Often made from pique cotton with ribbed cuffs.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A polo shirt without sleeves, combining the collar and placket formality of a polo with the freedom and ventilation of a tank top. Primarily seen in golf, tennis, and resort wear. Less common in men's fashion than women's.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

parameters.name: polo_type
parameters.description: The overall category or sub-type of polo shirt based on its design heritage, construction, and intended use

values.definition: The standard polo shirt with a ribbed collar, 2-3 button placket, and pique cotton body. The original sporting polo design pioneered by Rene Lacoste in the 1920s-30s. The foundation of the polo shirt category and the most widely recognized variant.
sources: Moda Knits - Types of Polo Shirts
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A heavier-weight, long-sleeve polo variant with reinforced stitching, a rigid woven collar, and a long front placket. Originally designed for the sport of rugby. Features heavyweight jersey fabric, often with horizontal stripes. Provides a rugged, casual aesthetic suited for fall/winter layering.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts
Moda Knits - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: An athletic-oriented polo made from technical fabrics with moisture-wicking, quick-dry, anti-odor, UV protection, and stretch properties. Designed for golf, tennis, and active lifestyles. Typically slim-fitted with functional features prioritized over traditional aesthetics.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts
The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide

values.definition: A polo constructed from a heavier, textured knit fabric (often wool or fine-gauge cotton) that provides a vintage-inspired, sweater-like appearance. Sits between casual and formal, offering more visual depth than a standard polo. Popular for smart casual and business casual contexts.
sources: The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A polo made from smooth, lightweight jersey knit rather than textured pique. Has a more relaxed, t-shirt-like drape and feel while retaining the polo's collar and placket structure. Ideal for travel, weekend wear, and casual settings where comfort is prioritized over structure.
sources: The Bear House - Polo Fabric Guide
The Fashionisto - Types of Polo Shirts

values.definition: A refined polo designed to substitute for a dress shirt in business-casual or smart-casual settings. Typically features a woven collar, mercerized cotton or fine-gauge knit, hidden placket, and a tailored fit. May include collar stays. Pairs with blazers and dress trousers.

parameters.name: polo_button_material
parameters.description: The material used for the buttons on a polo shirt placket, which serves as a quality and price-point indicator

values.definition: The most common and affordable button material for polo shirts. Available in a wide range of colors and finishes. Durable and easy to maintain but lacks the premium feel and visual depth of natural materials.

Buttons cut from the nacre (inner shell lining) of mollusks, offering a natural iridescent sheen and depth of color. A hallmark of high-quality polo construction. More fragile than plastic and horn but valued for their luminous, premium appearance. One of the most classic button materials.

Buttons made from natural animal horn, each unique in its patterning and coloring. Another classic, premium button material associated with quality craftsmanship. Durable with a rich, organic appearance that develops character over time.

parameters.name: tshirt_style_type
parameters.description: The overall design category or sub-type of t-shirt based on print, wash treatment, or design approach, particularly relevant to the Indian market

values.definition: A solid-colored t-shirt with no prints, graphics, or patterns. The most versatile type, serving as a wardrobe staple that can be dressed up or down. Works for layering, casual wear, and as a base for accessorizing.

Features printed images, artwork, illustrations, or photo-realistic designs on the fabric. Makes a bold visual statement and serves as a form of self-expression. Can range from band logos and pop culture references to abstract art and anime themes.

Features text, slogans, quotes, or bold typography as the primary design element. Popular for making statements, showing brand identity, or expressing humor and personality. A strong trend in the Indian market with bold typography styles.

Features horizontal, vertical, or diagonal stripes in contrasting colors. A classic pattern that adds visual interest while remaining relatively understated. Horizontal stripes can visually broaden the torso while vertical stripes create a lengthening effect.

A treatment where the fabric is washed with chemicals (or pumice stones soaked in bleach) to create an intentionally uneven, faded appearance with a vintage aesthetic. Popular in Indian streetwear, acid wash adds unique texture and a retro-contemporary character. Trending strongly in 2025.

A technique where the fabric is tied, folded, or scrunched and then dyed to create patterns of color swirls, spirals, or radiating designs. Each piece is somewhat unique. Associated with bohemian and festival aesthetics, gaining renewed popularity in casual and streetwear contexts.

Features two or more large sections of contrasting solid colors combined in a single garment. Creates a bold, modern look through the juxtaposition of distinct color panels rather than gradual blends or patterns.

Features traditional Indian motifs, block prints, paisley, mandala, or other culturally inspired patterns. An emerging trend in the Indian market that blends heritage aesthetics with modern t-shirt construction and fits.

parameters.name: casual_shirt_type
parameters.description: The category or style of casual shirt, defined by its construction, fabric, collar design, and intended use context. Covers the full spectrum of non-dress shirts for menswear.

values.definition: A shirt made from basket-weave oxford cloth fabric with a soft roll button-down collar. Durable yet soft, it bridges casual and smart-casual dressing. The quintessential preppy staple, invented by Brooks Brothers in 1896.

A short-sleeve, button-front shirt with an open, unstructured collar that lies flat against the chest (no collar band). Creates a notched V-neckline. Also called a revere collar shirt. Often features relaxed boxy fit and bold prints. Originated in 1950s Cuba for hot climates.

A variant of the camp collar with a slightly more structured V-shaped neckline and retro-inspired aesthetic. Terms 'camp collar' and 'Cuban collar' are often used interchangeably, though Cuban tends to imply a more vintage, louche silhouette with a boxy fit.

A shirt featuring a short stand-up collar band (1-2 inches high) without collar leaves or points. The edges slightly overlap or meet at center front. Inspired by traditional Chinese Qing dynasty attire. Provides a clean, minimal, modern look.

A casual shirt made from linen fabric, prized for its natural breathability, moisture-wicking properties, and textured hand-feel. Slight wrinkling is characteristic and considered part of the charm. Ideal for hot and humid climates including Indian summers.

A casual shirt constructed from denim twill-weave fabric. Versatile and durable, it ages well with unique wear patterns developing over time. Available in various washes from raw indigo to light bleached. Heavier than chambray.

A shirt made from chambray, a plain-weave fabric using single strands of colored and white yarn. Visually similar to denim but lighter, softer, and more breathable. Offers a classic blue hue without denim's heaviness. Suitable for warm and transitional weather.

A casual shirt made from brushed cotton or wool flannel fabric, known for its soft, napped texture and warmth. Often features plaid or check patterns, though solid colors exist. A cold-weather staple associated with rugged, outdoorsy style. Excellent for layering.

A collarless shirt with a round neckline and a short button placket (typically 3-5 buttons). Resembles a polo without the collar. Available in long and short sleeves, cotton or waffle-knit. Provides a laid-back, masculine look and works well as a layering piece.

A heavier-weight shirt designed to be worn as a light outer layer (also called a shacket or shirt jacket). Typically made from flannel, corduroy, wool blends, or heavy cotton. Features a boxier fit, often with chest pockets. Bridges the gap between shirt and jacket for transitional weather.

A short-sleeved casual shirt with a soft collar and a two-or-three-button placket. Typically made from pique cotton knit. Straddles the line between casual and smart-casual. A staple of sporty, preppy style.

A camp-collar shirt characterized by bold, tropical-themed prints (floral, palm, scenic). Made from lightweight fabrics like rayon, cotton, or silk. A subset of camp collar shirts with distinctly vacation/resort-inspired aesthetics.

A shirt with a simple fabric band encircling the neck instead of a traditional folded collar. Also called a grandad collar shirt. The band stands 1-2 inches high. Provides a clean, contemporary aesthetic suited to smart-casual occasions. Related to but distinct from the mandarin collar.

A modern hybrid garment blending the Indian kurta silhouette with Western shirt construction. Features a longer length, often with mandarin or band collar, side slits, and lightweight fabrics like linen or cotton. Popular for casual and festive occasions in the Indian market.

A casual shirt made from a blend of linen and cotton fibers, combining the breathability and texture of linen with the structure, softness, and durability of cotton. Popular in Indian and tropical markets for its balanced comfort properties.

A casual or smart-casual shirt made from poplin, a tightly-woven plain-weave fabric with a smooth finish. Lighter and crisper than oxford cloth. Often used for summer casual shirts and can range from fully casual to business-appropriate.

A casual shirt made from twill-weave fabric, identifiable by its diagonal ribbing. Heavier and more textured than poplin, softer than denim. Provides warmth and drape, making it suitable for cooler weather casual wear.
A casual shirt made from corduroy fabric featuring distinctive vertical ridges (wales). A warm-weather alternative to flannel with a distinctive texture. Often used in overshirt form for layering.

A casual button-front shirt made from knit jersey fabric rather than woven material. Combines the look of a traditional shirt with the stretch and comfort of a knit. Often used for travel and relaxed casual contexts.
A casual knit shirt featuring raglan sleeves (typically in a contrasting color) and a button placket. Named for its association with baseball uniforms. A distinctly casual, sporty piece.

parameters.name: casual_shirt_fit
parameters.description: The cut and silhouette of a casual shirt, determining how closely it follows the body's contours and where it falls on the torso.

values.definition: Tailored to follow the body's natural contours with minimal excess fabric. Sits closer to the body from chest to waist with narrower sleeves. Often features slight stretch for mobility. Creates a sharp, modern silhouette. Best for lean to average builds, smart-casual settings, and layering under blazers.

A balanced, moderate fit offering room across the chest, waist, and sleeves without being oversized. Straighter cut than slim fit. Versatile for everyday wear, works well both tucked and untucked. Suits a wide range of body shapes. Also called 'classic fit' by some brands.

A looser cut prioritizing freedom of movement and casual ease. Extra space in the torso, shoulders, and arms. Fabric drapes more freely rather than following body shape. Ideal for all-day comfort and laid-back styling. Works well in warmer climates where airflow is desired.

A deliberately roomy, boxy cut with significant extra volume throughout. Dropped shoulders and wider body. A trend-forward silhouette that pairs well with slim bottoms for contrast. Best styled tucked into slim jeans or with structured bottoms to avoid a shapeless look.

Not a body fit per se, but a specific length cut designed to be worn untucked. Front hem ends between the middle and bottom of the pants zipper; back hem ends between the middle and bottom of pants back pockets. Shorter than standard shirt length to avoid looking sloppy when worn out.

A fit designed for muscular or athletic builds, offering more room in the chest and shoulders while tapering through the waist. Prevents the pulling and bunching that standard slim fits cause on larger upper bodies.

parameters.name: casual_shirt_collar
parameters.description: The collar style on a casual shirt, which defines the neckline shape, formality level, and tie compatibility.

values.definition: A collar with small buttons fastening the collar points to the shirt front. Creates a soft, rolling collar shape. The quintessential casual-to-smart-casual collar. Invented by Brooks Brothers in 1896, inspired by English polo players. Can be worn with or without a tie, though the tie look is distinctly American preppy.

A flat, open collar with no collar band that lies against the chest, creating a notched V-neckline. Unstructured and never worn with a tie. The most casual collar type, associated with vacation and resort wear. Provides excellent ventilation in hot weather.

A short stand-up collar band (1-2 inches) without folded-over collar leaves. Edges may slightly overlap or meet at center. Rooted in traditional Chinese fashion. Projects a modern, minimalist aesthetic. Cannot accommodate a tie.

A simple fabric band encircling the neck without any collar points or leaves. Also called a grandad collar. Similar to mandarin but sometimes slightly shorter and without the characteristic slight overlap. A smart-casual choice that captures contemporary informality.

A collar with wider-set points creating a broad opening. The casual version uses softer construction (no collar stays) compared to dress shirt spreads. Versatile enough for open-neck casual wear or with a tie for smart-casual. Flatters most face shapes.

The most traditional collar with narrow, pointed tips angled downward. In casual shirts, often made with softer construction than dress versions. Creates a slimming effect, making it suitable for wider faces and shorter necks.

A collar with small, rounded points instead of sharp tips. Has a vintage, early 20th-century aesthetic. Originally designed for evening wear but now used in casual and smart-casual contexts for its retro appeal.

A collarless round neckline with a short button placket (typically 3-5 buttons). Not technically a collar but a distinct neckline treatment found on henley shirts. Provides casual masculinity without any collar structure.

parameters.name: jeans_fit
parameters.description: The overall silhouette and cut of men's jeans, defined by the width through the seat, thigh, knee, and leg opening. The primary classification parameter for jeans.

values.definition: The narrowest fit, sitting tight from hip to ankle with a very slim leg opening (typically 12-14 inches). Hugs the legs closely throughout. Associated with indie/rock aesthetics and experiencing a revival via the 'indie sleaze' trend. Best for lean builds.

A modern, tapered fit that is snug through the thigh and knee but not skin-tight. Leg opening typically 14-16 inches. Provides a sharp silhouette without the extremity of skinny. The go-to fit for men who want a put-together look. Works for most body types except very muscular thighs.

Wider through the thigh for comfort, then gradually narrows from the knee to the ankle. Combines relaxed room up top with a tailored lower leg. Ideal for men with athletic or muscular thighs who want a contemporary look. The 'best of both worlds' fit.

A consistent width from the hip down to the ankle with no taper. The most classic, timeless jeans silhouette. Versatile enough to dress up or down. Works well for most body types. The leg opening matches the knee width.

A moderate fit that is neither slim nor relaxed, offering comfortable room through the seat and thigh with a straight or slightly tapered leg. Often used as a brand's default or standard fit. Very similar to straight but may have slightly more room in the seat.

A loose, comfortable fit with extra room in the seat, thigh, and leg. Sits comfortably without clinging to the body. Gaining momentum in 2025 as casual comfort takes priority. Best for larger builds or those prioritizing ease of movement.

Fitted through the thigh, then gradually widens from the knee to the hem to accommodate boots. The leg opening is wider than the knee (typically 18-20 inches). A classic American style experiencing a clean, modern revival in 2025. Helps balance wider shoulders and hips.

Specifically designed for muscular or athletic builds. Relaxed through the hip and thigh for room around muscular legs, then tapers below the knee for a modern look. Essentially a tapered fit with extra thigh room. Fills the gap between slim and relaxed for built physiques.

A roomy fit with significant width from thigh to hem, creating a dramatic, flowing silhouette. Sits on the hips with a relaxed fit throughout. A trend-forward style in 2025 associated with vintage and streetwear aesthetics. Often features shorter inseams designed to stack.

An extremely loose fit with maximum room throughout the seat, thigh, and leg. More voluminous than relaxed fit. Associated with 1990s streetwear and hip-hop culture. Trending in 2025 with a more structured, intentional approach compared to the original 90s versions.

A hybrid fit combining the narrower proportions of slim with the consistent leg width of straight. Slimmer through the thigh than standard straight but without the dramatic taper of slim fit. A versatile middle ground.

A hybrid combining the close fit of slim jeans with aggressive tapering toward the ankle. Tighter overall than standard tapered. Creates the most streamlined modern silhouette while still offering some thigh room.

parameters.name: jeans_wash
parameters.description: The wash treatment applied to denim, which determines the color intensity, surface texture, and aesthetic character of the jeans. Ranges from untreated raw denim to heavily processed distressed styles.

values.definition: Completely untreated denim in its most natural state, with no washing, fading, or distressing. Also called 'dry denim.' Features a rich, deep indigo hue and stiff, structured feel. Molds to the wearer's body over time, developing personalized fades, creases, and whisker patterns. Prized by denim purists.

Denim that has undergone a single, minimal wash to remove excess indigo dye and soften the fabric slightly. Also called 'mill wash' or 'one wash.' Produces the darkest available wash after raw. Clean, uniform appearance. The most versatile dark denim for smart-casual dressing.

Denim with minimal processing, preserving the deep indigo shade. May include a gentle rinse to remove excess dye. The most versatile wash: easily dressed up (with blazer) or down (with t-shirt). Slimming visual effect. Hides stains well.

Denim treated to sit between dark and light, showing moderate fading while retaining structure. The most 'classic jeans' look. Versatile and approachable, mixing easily with color and pattern. Hides small stains better than light wash.

Heavily faded denim with a pale, sun-bleached appearance. Created through extended stone washing or bleaching processes. Associated with relaxed, casual vibes. Particularly popular in summer. Can read as very casual or vintage depending on styling.

Denim treated by tumbling with pumice stones to soften the fabric and create an evenly worn-in, faded appearance. A classic technique popularized in the 1980s. Produces a softer hand-feel than raw or rinse denim. Can range from light to medium fading.

An eco-friendly alternative to stone washing using biological enzymes (cellulase) to break down indigo dye. Creates a faded look without harsh chemicals or physical abrasion. Produces a softer feel while causing less fiber damage than stone washing, extending garment lifespan.

Denim treated with pumice stones pre-soaked in bleach solution (not actual acid). Creates high-contrast, non-uniform marbling and splotchy patterns. Originally popularized in the 1980s. A bold, statement-making wash that cycles in and out of fashion.

Denim soaked in diluted bleach solution to strip color uniformly. Produces a lighter, evenly faded appearance ranging from light blue to nearly white. Unlike acid wash, creates uniform lightening rather than high-contrast marbling.

A treatment (not a color wash) featuring intentional rips, tears, frayed edges, and abraded areas for an edgy, lived-in aesthetic. Achieved through manual ripping, laser distressing, sandblasting, or enzyme washing. Can be applied over any wash color. Associated with grunge and streetwear.

Denim dyed with black (sulfur) dye rather than traditional indigo. Can range from jet black to faded charcoal. Black denim is versatile for evening and smart-casual wear. Tends to fade faster than indigo unless specially treated (overdyed or coated).

Denim that has been dyed a second time over its original indigo base with another color (often black, grey, or other hues). Creates deeper, richer color with a unique tonal quality. As the overdye wears off with use, the original indigo may show through.

A wash designed to replicate the naturally aged, worn-in appearance of old denim. Combines techniques like enzyme washing, whiskering, and strategic fading to simulate years of wear. Often features honeycomb fading behind knees and whisker lines at the hip crease.

A surface treatment producing thin, faded lines (whiskers) across the jeans, simulating natural crease patterns. Created by hand using abrasive rods or via laser. Applied around areas known to naturally crease: across thighs and behind knees. Often combined with other wash treatments.

A modern, sustainable technique using lasers to burn off indigo dye, creating precise fading and whiskering effects without water, stones, or chemicals. Allows highly detailed and reproducible patterns. Increasingly used by premium and eco-conscious brands.

parameters.name: jeans_rise
parameters.description: The vertical distance from the crotch seam to the top of the waistband, determining where jeans sit on the body and creating the perceived waistline.

values.definition: Rise measurement of 7-8 inches. Waistband sits near the top of the hip bones, well below the navel. Creates a contemporary, casual silhouette. Best for men with long legs and shorter torsos, or athletic builds. Can appear disproportionate on shorter men. The most casual rise option.

Rise measurement of 9-11 inches. Also called regular or normal rise. Waistband sits at or just below the navel at the natural waist. The most universally flattering rise, suiting virtually all body types. The default for most modern jeans including Levi's 501, slim fits, and athletic fits. Comfortable for all-day wear.

Rise measurement of 10-12+ inches. Waistband sits above the navel, covering it. Often called high-waisted. Creates a sophisticated, retro-inspired look. Elongates the appearance of legs, making it beneficial for both shorter and taller men. Minimizes muffin top appearance. More comfortable around the waist and less likely to slide down.

parameters.name: jeans_leg_shape
parameters.description: The shape of the jeans leg from the knee down, which is a sub-component of overall fit but a useful standalone parameter for precise classification.

values.definition: The leg narrows progressively from the knee to the ankle, creating a smaller leg opening. The most modern leg shape. Flattering on most builds as it creates a clean silhouette at the ankle.
Consistent leg width from knee to ankle with no narrowing or widening. The most classic, timeless leg shape. The leg opening matches or is very close to the knee width.
The leg widens significantly from the knee to the hem, creating a bell or trumpet shape. More dramatic than bootcut. Associated with 1970s fashion and periodic revival cycles.
A subtle widening from the knee to the hem, enough to comfortably fit over boot shafts. Less dramatic than a full flare. The functional leg shape for wearing jeans over cowboy boots or work boots.

A generously wide leg from knee to hem, creating a flowing, voluminous silhouette. Associated with streetwear, vintage Americana, and Japanese denim culture. Often designed with shorter inseams to create stacking.

parameters.name: jeans_body_type_mapping
parameters.description: A guide mapping body types to recommended jeans fits, based on proportional considerations from multiple sources.

values.definition: Slender frame with narrow hips, thighs, and waist. Recommended fits: skinny, slim, or slim-tapered to complement the frame without excess fabric. Avoid very wide or baggy cuts that can overwhelm the silhouette.

Well-developed thighs, glutes, and calves with a defined waist. Recommended fits: athletic fit, tapered, or relaxed-tapered that provide thigh room while tapering below the knee. Slim fits may restrict and pull across the quads.

Balanced proportions without extreme muscle development or leanness. Recommended fits: straight, regular, or slim-straight offer the most versatility. Virtually any fit works, making personal style preference the deciding factor.

Broader frame with fuller hips, thighs, and waist. Recommended fits: relaxed, straight, or bootcut provide comfort and balanced proportions. Bootcut helps balance wider hips and shoulders. Avoid very slim or skinny fits that restrict movement and create pulling.

Height 6 feet or above with longer legs and torso. Recommended rise: high rise to sit at the right part of a longer waist. Any leg shape works, but straight and tapered are most universally flattering. Look for extended inseam options.

Below-average height with proportionally shorter legs. Recommended: high-rise jeans to elongate the leg line. Tapered or slim fits create a streamlined look. Avoid low-rise which shortens the leg visually. Avoid excessively wide or bootcut fits that can overwhelm shorter frames.

parameters.name: casual_trouser_type
parameters.description: The category/style of casual trousers or pants, distinguishing between different silhouettes, constructions, and intended use cases

values.definition: Lightweight cotton twill trousers with hidden stitching and a tapered, form-fitting cut. Originated from the 1898 Spanish-American War when soldiers improvised uniforms using Chinese twill cotton. Strikes a balance between casual and formal, suitable for business-casual to casual settings.

Cotton twill trousers with visible stitching and pockets, offering a more relaxed fit than chinos. Heavier, thicker cotton twill fabric with a sturdy workwear heritage. Name derived from Persian for 'dust', originating from British military uniforms in 19th-century India.

Modern evolution of sweatpants with elastic or drawstring waist and close-fitting leg that tapers to elasticated cuffs. Made from softer fabrics like fleece, cotton, or tech materials. Offers a streamlined, athletic-casual silhouette compared to traditional sweatpants.

Rugged cotton or cotton-blend trousers featuring multiple large utility pockets on the legs. Military-inspired design originating from 1938 British army and later adopted by US military in WWII. The most storage-friendly pant style.

Lightweight, breathable trousers made from linen fabric, ideal for warm weather and summer occasions. Ultra-breathable, naturally cooling, with a relaxed drape. Suited for resort, travel, and minimalist summer looks.

Casual trousers with an elastic or drawstring waistband instead of a traditional button/zip closure. Offers maximum comfort with easy fit adjustment. Often made from linen, cotton, or blended fabrics.
Trousers made from corduroy fabric featuring distinctive raised parallel ridges (wales). Available in various wale widths from fine to wide. A textured alternative to chinos suited for autumn/winter.

Lightweight trousers made from puckered seersucker fabric, traditionally in blue-and-white stripes. The puckered texture allows airflow, making them ideal for hot weather. A preppy, summer-specific option.
Soft, loose-fitting athletic trousers with elastic waist and often elastic cuffs. Made from fleece or jersey cotton. Primarily loungewear or athletic wear, less streamlined than joggers.

Hybrid style combining the polished look of chinos with the elastic waist and tapered cuffs of joggers. Offers a contemporary option that transitions from casual weekends to informal business meetings.

Wide-leg, relaxed-fit trousers inspired by Korean fashion trends. Often features a high waist, pleated front, and generous drape through the leg. A fashion-forward alternative to traditional relaxed-fit trousers.

parameters.name: casual_trouser_fit
parameters.description: The silhouette and cut of casual trousers, determining how closely the fabric follows the body from waist to ankle

values.definition: Cut closer to the body throughout the leg creating a sleek, modern silhouette. Pairs well with fitted blazers and dress shirts. Best suited for lean to average builds.

Features a gradual narrowing from the thigh to the ankle, offering room at the hip and thigh while maintaining a clean ankle line. A contemporary balance between classic and slim fits, versatile for both professional and casual settings.
Consistent width from the thigh through the leg opening with no tapering. The most traditional and universally flattering silhouette. A balanced look that works for most body types.
Looser cut through the seat and thigh area providing maximum ease of movement and comfort. A more traditional, generous fit ideal for casual settings and weekend wear. Works well for broader frames.

Roomier through the thigh and seat to accommodate muscular builds, then tapering to a narrower leg opening. Designed for men with larger thighs relative to waist. Combines comfort with a modern silhouette.

The most traditional silhouette with a straight leg and comfortable room throughout. Sits at the natural waist and provides a balanced look that flatters most body types without being too loose or too fitted.

Trousers that end above the ankle, creating a modern, fashion-forward look. Works particularly well in warmer weather and when styled with loafers or sneakers. Often combined with slim or tapered cuts.

parameters.name: casual_trouser_rise
parameters.description: The distance from the crotch seam to the top of the waistband, affecting comfort, proportions, and visual leg length

values.definition: Waistband sits at or above the natural waist. Elongates the legs visually and provides a more classic, polished appearance. Comfortable for most body types.
Waistband sits between the hip bone and the natural waist. The most common and versatile rise, offering a balanced silhouette suitable for most occasions.
Waistband sits below the hip bone. Offers a casual, contemporary vibe. Can visually shorten the legs and is best suited for taller frames.

parameters.name: casual_trouser_color
parameters.description: The predominant color of casual trousers, affecting versatility, formality, and outfit coordination

values.definition: Deep blue tone that is among the most versatile chino colors. Pairs well with a variety of blazers and dress shirts. Appropriate for any occasion and easily dressed up or down. Contrasts nicely with lighter tops.
The original and most traditional chino color, a dusty tan derived from the Persian word for 'dust'. Highly versatile neutral that pairs with most colors. A wardrobe essential.

Dark grey tone that is among the most versatile trouser colors alongside navy. Pairs with a wide range of tops and can read as semi-formal. A sophisticated neutral suitable for office and evening wear.
Medium grey offering a contemporary, modern aesthetic. Works well in chino jogger styles. Transitions easily from casual weekends to informal business settings.
Military-inspired green-brown tone that adds visual interest while remaining neutral enough for versatile pairing. A classic casual trouser color with outdoor and heritage connotations.
Light, warm neutral tone similar to beige or sand. A lighter alternative to khaki that works well in spring/summer. Pairs easily with most tops.
The darkest neutral, offering maximum versatility and a sleek, modern appearance. Can read as more formal than other casual trouser colors. A wardrobe staple.
Light, summer-appropriate color that creates a clean, fresh look. Best suited for warm weather and resort settings. Requires more care to maintain.
A bold, rich color option that adds personality to an outfit. Best balanced with neutral tops (white, grey, navy). A seasonal autumn/winter accent color.

parameters.name: shorts_type
parameters.description: The category/style of men's shorts, distinguishing between different constructions, pocket configurations, and intended use cases

values.definition: Tailored shorts made from cotton twill with a polished, clean finish. Sharp and classy, suitable for lunch dates and relaxed days out. Often feature a flat front and welt or slant pockets. Pair well with polos, casual tees, sneakers, or loafers.

Performance-oriented shorts made from moisture-wicking polyester blends. Typically feature an elastic waist, lightweight construction, and quick-dry properties. Often end 5-6 inches above the knee. Designed for workouts, running, and gym activities.

Casual shorts featuring multiple large utility pockets on the legs. Made from sturdy cotton blends for durability. Popular across all ages for their functionality, ideal for hiking, outdoor activities, and casual wear.

Swim-specific shorts made from nylon with a mesh inner lining for quick drying. Available as shorter trunks with elastic waistband or longer boardshorts with a front opening. Designed specifically for water activities.
Shorts cut from denim fabric, either manufactured or cut from full-length jeans. Casual summer staple with a relaxed, laid-back aesthetic. Best suited for very casual settings.
Lightweight, breathable shorts made from linen fabric. Extremely skin-friendly and ideal for warm weather. Look great on weekend getaways and at seaside resorts. A summer wardrobe necessity.
Chino shorts with added elastane for flexibility and comfort. Popular in shorter inseams (5-inch). Combines the polished look of traditional chinos with modern comfort technology.

parameters.name: shorts_length
parameters.description: The inseam length of shorts relative to the knee, affecting both aesthetics and occasion-appropriateness

values.definition: Shorts ending 2-3 inches above the knee (typically 5-7 inch inseam). The most recommended length for casual shorts with t-shirts, button-downs, or polos. Creates a balanced, modern look.
Shorts ending at mid-thigh (typically 5 inch inseam or shorter). Common for athletic and swim shorts. A fashion-forward length that works best on taller or leaner frames.
Shorts ending right at the kneecap (typically 9-10 inch inseam). A more conservative, traditional length. Common in cargo shorts and older chino short styles.
Shorts ending below the kneecap (11+ inch inseam). Common in boardshorts and some cargo styles. Generally considered a dated or sport-specific length in modern menswear.

parameters.name: casual_jacket_type
parameters.description: The category/style of men's casual jackets and outerwear, distinguishing between different heritage origins, constructions, and silhouettes
